newsitem.title: USA: Reno opposes immunity for Huang, Thompson says.
newsitem.headline: Reno opposes immunity for Huang, Thompson says.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno opposes granting limited immunity from prosecution to John Huang, a central figure in the Democratic campaign fund-raising scandal, the chairman of the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee said Wednesday.
The chairman, Tennessee Republican Sen. Fred Thompson, said the committee would make its own decision on granting limited immunity to Huang and would continue negotiations with Huang's attorney.

Huang has offered to testify to the committee's investigation into Democratic fund-raising practices from the 1996 campaigns if the committee will give him immunity from prosecution on possible violations of campaign finance laws or any other charges except espionage and passing secrets to foreign countries.
Thompson said he received word from Reno that she opposed immunity to Huang. Her Justice Department is conducting its own investigation into the fund-raising controversy.

Sen. John Glenn, the Ohio Democrat who is senior minority member of the committee, said he hoped the committee can "figure out a way to give him protection in fairly small areas" so he can give his side of the story.

Committee members said Huang's attorney, Ty Cobb, should submit a description of what Huang is prepared to tell the committee in return for limited immunity. A meeting between committee lawyers and Huang's attorney is scheduled for Friday, Thompson said.
